notes.title: Monthly Development Update - July 2025
notes.content:
[p]This month has been all about momentum. Planets, missions, and the systems that tie it all together. Our third Planet (official name incoming) is well underway, with fresh terrain, environmental effects, and some seriously mind-bending rocks and trees. Facility design is expanding fast, and our mission system is starting to feel fully alive..[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/08654957339491d71802b7ee76f1a20396a5e5df.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Players will notice smoother targeting, better feedback, new HUD elements, and dynamic music shifts that respond to gameplay. We’ve also implemented mission loading screens, real-time death drops, and refined how Facilities rotate on the Mission Map.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/61b1e0e0d5678bf2ee7f07811a029205e9d09ec5.jpg"][/img][/p][p]
Meanwhile, behind the scenes, we’ve been optimizing just about everything, from material meshes to how Facility maps stream in and out. Beamable now manages all mission and planet state data.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d8b71491f567b46a7ea049e2b020b5e1e2f27e18.jpg"][/img][/p][p]And of course, with [url="https://www.gamescom.global/en"]gamescom[/url] 2025 on the horizon, we’ve been laying the groundwork for a big showing, tightening our GTM plan, while we prepare for our closed Beta launch.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/7b36e33f805925b97ef06c687fb36cd0c93f96fd.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Let’s get into it.[/h3]

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - June 2025
notes.content: [p]Another month in the bag here at Warped, and this month was heavily focused on gameplay and player experience. Gameplay, progression, maps, enemies, loadouts, and almost all other areas of where games become “fun” were leveled up this month. There was a point where everyone on the team started talking about how it suddenly was more fun and it felt rewarding to play. It wasn’t just testing, it was enjoyable.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/e7dda7104383594125b1822c7df4a4fdcd033e06.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve been aiming to reach this point in internal testing and development before moving on to our next phase, which involves bringing in outside testers for a closed beta. We want testers to enjoy the experience and feel like their actions matter, so that they stick around and continue to play, rather than test and grind. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/06b5a3684c815e1556434563e1f1564224b61f55.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We believe that the results of a happy tester will have a much more lasting impact in the long run. While there are still some engineering milestones to hit before closed beta, the fun has already begun, and it will help closed beta be more impactful once started.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8c01d8aae9e0f4cf51f661bc06f25f7a6c034d7f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]One of the major standouts in the update is how the game now loads maps, facilities, and enemies in a more dynamic and random fashion, resulting in gameplay that constantly changes and evolves throughout each mission. To do this, we needed more maps and facilities to load. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/14c0bfe2d1328f4f859ec95fc2661264897fe53d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Besides all the new facilities and parts that were designed, our artists created a new planet, one that is incredibly unique and unlike than anything we’ve seen in a game before. It feels dreamlike, and the influences from old sci-fi films and books are coming in full throttle.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/554f2bb59574a9555a74001535f51357680e1981.jpg"][/img][/p][p]When we first brainstormed Warped Universe, we made a pact to create a universe that stands out. We want every screenshot to scream Warped Universe. This new planet and map do that more than ever before. We’re making a fun, exciting, and fresh game, and we’re beyond thrilled to be at this point in development.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/20eca8f9c3c6ca452e7d80018c1a093693aca5fd.jpg"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - May 2025
notes.content:
We covered all fronts this month at Warped Games, from game dev to marketing to backend infrastructure. One of the biggest wins was the momentum we’ve seen on our Steam page. We’ve spent the past six months consistently updating it with new content, visuals, and community posts. That kind of work doesn’t pay off immediately, it takes time, iteration, and a lot of convincing to get people to hit that Wishlist button. But this month, it clicked.

Thanks to a strong marketing push, more eyes are landing on Warped Universe, and more people are deciding it’s worth a spot on their wishlist. What’s even more exciting is that those numbers are now growing organically, players are discovering the game through other Steam pages, features, and community recommendations. That’s hugely rewarding, and we’ll keep building on that visibility with regular updates and gameplay reveals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0fc41f40221a09f57c92fc20a4c0879b3aa3bca1.png[/img]
This month we focused heavily on ships, both player and Void. Void ships used to be simple palette-swapped versions of player ships. That’s now completely changed. Our art and design teams worked together to create an entirely new aesthetic for the Void, pulling more from their origin in the lore and pushing them into something far more eerie and distinct. The new models look truly warped and hostile, exactly as they should!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9dfa4309393c8103a9dbb93468d6c002b363b0e4.jpg[/img]
Player ships got a major upgrade too. We added loads of new cosmetic parts (like sails, tails, tusks, wings, hulls, masks, and auras), and reworked ship materials across all five battlepass tiers. These changes give players much more control over their visual identity in the universe. We also introduced new aura FX and a modular base system for internal ship skeletons to support even more variations in the future.

A lot of time this month went into tightening gameplay systems and combat feedback. Ammo was removed from player weapons to streamline combat, and damage numbers have been added for both player and enemy hits. This alone makes encounters feel more readable and reactive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/adf4c006f9b7ee20299a36d495bc6a999430a96a.png[/img]
On the backend side, we synced our latest work with Beamable and continued expanding tools and systems for development. Niagara FX scripts and emitters were pushed to handle new skeletal effects, and we laid the groundwork for future mission interactions by building a flexible base to build them on top of.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8cdc2c173da17d46d3ed071f7cba6ce3c2e2394c.png[/img]
That’s it for this month’s game development update. We’re making Warped Universe deeper, sharper, and more reactive across the board. Thanks for continuing to follow the journey, whether you're here for the lore, the systems, or just to watch the ships explode in style, we’re glad you’re along for the ride.

[b]Wishlist us on Steam if you haven’t already, and let us know what you think in the comments or on Discord![/b]

notes.title: The Living Map of the Warped Universe
notes.content:
[i]"The System Status Map is a direct projection of the state of our sprawling and fragile environment. As the frontier’s pylons are built and stabilized, sector matter and energy is directly reflected in real time here in the center of Nexus Station. Part model, part news broadcast, part mission board. It's the focus of every warp pioneer, these warped particles entangled at a tiny ratio with the chaos out there. It's the pulse - the vital signs of the star system, and thus we must all monitor it closely."[/i]
[b]- Dr Monica Monos[/b]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

While many parts of Nexus Station help prepare a player for their journey, one in particular shows them where their actions truly matter. That’s the System Status Map, a massive interactive map of the known universe, displaying live data, and real-time player influence.
At the heart of the monitor is the system’s sun. More than just a visual set piece, the star reflects the Balance of Light and Gravity, a global system mechanic that shifts based on collective player behavior. Each mission you complete tips the scales in one direction or the other.
As the balance shifts further in either direction, certain changes in gameplay occur, movement speed, resistances, damage and skills are all affected

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3bfd9b3f018576f929790d3481657cc793e330ed.jpg[/img]
Every visual marker is interactive, offering mission options, cooperative goals, and strategic alerts. Whether you're soloing a scout mission or teaming up to contain a Void outbreak, your actions feed into this living display, and the monitor updates in real time..

The System Map shows not just where you can go, but why it matters. Players can see:
[list]
[*] Planets - Both completed and in construction
[*] Facilities on planets - Showing how developed or vulnerable they are
[*] Unmapped sectors - Explore mission areas obscured by Void interference
[*] Active void tears - Unstable zones where enemy invasions are occurring
[*] Pylon networks - Vital objectives required to stabilize new regions and expand the system
[*] Residuum Deposits - Collection and Transport missions required to facilitate the construction of Planets
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9a3d170d37f1d8d8811e5066d69cf14eadc7f8b4.jpg[/img]
Each facility type adds significant benefits and opportunities upon completion that remain as long as the facility is operational. 

Facility upgrades include:
[list]
[*] Farm Facilities - Provide a health bonus to players embarking on missions
[*] Housing Facilities - Adds choice and reduces costs of end of mission rewards
[*] Power Facilities - Increases the rarity of mission rewards
[*] Factory Facilities - Adds the possibility of rolling certain attributes on equipment obtained from Artifractal Cores
[*] Research Facilities - Increase the Potential of any new piece of equipment in that category 
[*] Spaceport Facilities - Required to kick start a new planet once discovered and constructed
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0c81f5bacdafac2774bdae36918118d0d58871e5.jpg[/img]
Each of these upgrades is improved further as more of each type of facility is completed throughout the system, changing gameplay options significantly from start of season to the end. 

There’s a strange sensation when using the System Monitor: you feel like a miniature piece on a galactic game board. And in some sense, you are. But unlike a traditional game, the board is unfinished, unmapped, and at risk.
This is what makes the SSM feel alive: it doesn't just reflect the state of the game, it is the state of the game.

The System Status Map turns abstract player behavior into visible consequence. It tracks a shared universe, responds to individual decisions, and serves as the connective tissue for strategy, cooperation, and survival.

It’s not just where you get missions. It’s where you see your impact. Every new region you open, every planet that forms, every moment of collapse or recovery... it all echoes on this surface.

notes.title: Your First 60 Minutes In Warped Universe
notes.content:
[i]“Transition into the Warped Universe is not merely geographic, it is existential. Individuals who volunteer for traversal are often driven by complex emotional and psychological motivations that include the desire for redemption, escape, or transformation. Understanding these motivations is crucial for the ongoing development of civilian acclimation protocols, therapeutic interventions, and mission suitability assessments.
As humanity continues to spread into new dimensions, it must also reckon with the psychological cost of leaving Earth behind, not just the world, but the self that belonged to it.”[/i]
[b] - Dr. Elira Senn
 Civilian Wellness Division, Celadon Station[/b]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/c6f9253e97cc4d9d14b8cdbb1fe1009398566d09.jpg[/img]
So you’ve just stepped through the portal on Celadon Station. The world you knew is far behind, and ahead lies a station held together by ingenuity, stubbornness, and something stranger. Welcome to the Warped Universe.

Let’s take a look at what to expect in your first hour aboard Nexus Station. Whether you’re a veteran of sci-fi adventures or just curious what you’ve signed up for, here’s how your journey begins.
Your first steps on Nexus Station follow a 15-minute introduction through a vision of the recent past, the fall of Embry’s Hope, the first world consumed by the Void.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d437a83e7c5a7b83cec48038508704ab1689b2a5.jpg[/img]
In this playable prologue, you’ll experience four core game modes:
[list]
[*] Third-person ground combat 
[*] Turn-based ground tactics
[*] Real-time space action
[*] Turn-based space strategy
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/4461ba3b11bb35381a86f88784506534b468f76d.jpg[/img]
You’ll escort fleeing scientists, try out your first skill, clear asteroid paths for evac ships, and dogfight hostile fighters in orbit. As the planet collapses around you, you witness its final moments.

Then, everything goes white.

As your consciousness rethreads itself, your body begins to reassemble, this time by choice. This is where you define who you are in the Warped Universe. Appearance, name, core traits, this is your moment to shape your identity.
You open your own eyes once more to the pristine interior of Nexus Station, and your journey truly begins.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3bfd9b3f018576f929790d3481657cc793e330ed.jpg[/img]
After a moment introducing yourself on Nexus, you’ll be thrown right back into the action, this time, it’s your choice of what type of mission you play and how you play it. Completing this, you’ll receive your first Artifractal Core, and learn to make your first piece of equipment, then it's back to the mission map to take on another challenge before receiving a Spark and learning how to upgrade your gear. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/006ae5f0e11343fad13e84fb1e8b0b238b708457.jpg[/img]
Next, you’ll be introduced to the two primary ideologies on Nexus Station. The Foundationalists focus on stability, order, and rebuilding what was lost. The Luminaries seek insight, exploration, and the expansion of what’s known in the Warped Universe. You’ll learn how to gain reputation with both of them through mission choices, unlocking rewards, new challenges, and your place in the social fabric of the station.

[h3]Now it’s game on.[/h3]

Your goal in Warped Universe is to rebuild what was lost after a cosmic catastrophe fractured reality itself. As a survivor and explorer arriving through the portal to Nexus Station, you join the effort to reclaim the galaxy from the chaos of the Void.  Along the way, you'll build your strength, uncover ancient truths, and shape the future of this strange new cosmos.
Your main enemies are entities born from the collapse of the old universe, shaped by fear, memory, and instability. These creatures are unpredictable, often terrifying reflections of what was, or what might have been. They will challenge both your combat skills and your understanding of the universe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9e67b9f6ddd680926835deea4168e43551c5d84e.jpg[/img]
Victory isn’t determined by a single event, it’s a long-term journey that involves rebuilding habitable planets, securing territory from Void influence, and strengthening your loadout through Sparks and Cores.
In the future, large-scale collaborative goals and factional conflicts may further define what “winning” means.
From here, you’re free to pursue missions at your pace, upgrade your kit, and learn how the balance of Light and Gravity shapes every encounter.
You’ve got a long road ahead, but your first steps? You’ve taken them..

[h3]Welcome to Warped Universe.[/h3]

notes.title: Unfolding Artifractals
notes.content:
[i]“There was a time when we thought the entire warped universe was nothing but stray pockets of particle concentration and massive, scattered fields of inert residuum. As our earliest researchers collected and refined residuum into a usable form they encountered rare deposits of more complex amalgamations of matter. These pieces of crystalized power actually caused a great deal of damage to the processing equipment upon their discovery. The internal reflective surfaces are of a varied complexity with an expected increase in energetic potency. We dubbed them Artifractal Cores. Bring me one of those and watch the tech do the rest.”[/i]

[b]- First Techsmith
[/b]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Along with Sparks, Nexite, and battlepass XP, Artifractal Cores are one of the end of mission rewards available to choose to progress along your journey in Warped Universe. 
Artifractal Cores, or Cores as they are obviously going to be referred to, are the resource allowing players to acquire new equipment.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f5e339b2a7c51dc8588f81e9f0835559b598386f.jpg[/img]
Artifractal Cores, or simply “Cores”,  are the basic element required for all weapon and gear crafting in Warped Universe. Since all specialization and stat boosting will be carried out by gear rather than a standard character level-up mechanic, Cores are the foundation and framework of any player loadout. From tanky brawler sets to fast and accurate pieces, (or any combinations in between) the gear built at an Artifractal Core table will provide the player a vast combination of strengths and strategies.
Cores can be obtained in six rarities, common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary and Warped. The power of any given core is easily predicted by the complexity of its shape.
After receiving a Core, the player must take it to the Artifractal Core table in Nexus Station and choose the equipment you want or need at the time. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/42cbcdfa5ce4f5d8495f54754428e1a577fbc46f.jpg[/img]
When you use a Core table, you’ll be faced with a few choices. First you select whether you want equipment for your ground character or your space ship, armor or weapon, then specifically which piece you want to receive for each loadout. 
You may want a new ship hull for example, go to the table, select ship, then hull, choose your core rarity and hope for the best. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/41128460ffbe74051e75cfc18b02d474b678efaf.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/90ce3f0e65d3c0a37df286de17bc575a99b68204.jpg[/img]
Each piece of equipment comes with its own appearance and base modifiers that will remain the same regardless of Core rarity. There will be equipment with modifiers weighted in all directions, ensuring you have the ability to create multiple loadouts for any scenario.
The benefit of a higher Core rarity is the significant number of desirable bonus modifiers on a piece of equipment. These stat types are randomized from the list of upgrades available from Planet Facility unlocks. 

Modifiers in Warped Universe currently include:

[b]Power[/b] - Reducing weapon recoil and increasing critical strike damage.
[b]Precision[/b] - Increasing accuracy and critical strike chance.
[b]Psionics[/b] - Used to increase skill usage in the form of cool down reduction, skill range, and AoE size.
[b]Health[/b]- Increasing base health points.
[b]Speed[/b] - Increasing movement speed, by percentage in action modes and tiles moved in turn-based.
[b]Dodge[/b] - Decreases the possibility of being hit.
[b]Resists[/b] - Reduces damage received. Comes in the form of armor piercing, kinetic, light, gravity, and void.
[b]Additional Damage Dice[/b] - Increases damage done, and potentially varying the damage types you deal.
[b]Potential[/b] - The resource players spend to further upgrade their equipment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8cde12d16b68b1de649ef5f32b9dc88b6eee05c2.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0e38b69b8df8d90e43e3e27431d0e6d77ae9f02a.jpg[/img]
Cores also serve a secondary purpose, allowing players to reset upgrade potential on a piece of equipment, but we’ll get into that later.

The Artifractal Core system provides an opportunity for the player to stay connected to their in-game character regardless of how they want to change or accentuate their playstyle. It provides a frictionless and interesting way to min-max their loadout without abandoning any previous progress. 

Customize your experience, choose your pace, and as always… 

[h3]Play Your Way[/h3]

notes.title: The Constant Conflict
notes.content:
[i]"The endless challenges of propagating a secure population include the construction and maintenance of strange, technically wondrous feats of engineering while beset by a ceaseless tide of invasion. After a time, one yearns for the drudgery of monotonous tasks when the spectre of destruction lurks around every corner. But just as we strive for balance in the universal forces, we must also balance our efforts between the impressive and the inane. The perils are seemingly insurmountable, but the rewards defy imagination. We do what we do not only for the bounty of victory, but also because it is the right thing to do."[/i]
[b]- Orin[/b]

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

At its core, Warped Universe is a battle for creation and survival faced with the constant threat of annihilation. The remnants of a shattered civilization drift over silent distances, caught between the fluctuating forces of Light and Gravity. Players travel to the ruins of this universe, re-shaping its fate through strategic exploration, planetary construction, and high intensity battles.
Missions run the full gamut between complex infiltrations of construction areas on the untamed frontier to simple data collection goals in sparsely infested farmlands. Regardless of the setting and threat, each excursion into the young system’s environments brings a variety of challenges and strategies. Players can always choose a threat level and pace that appeals to their gaming senses.
Our conflict extends beyond simple good versus evil. It’s a struggle of balance, where every action shifts the cosmic scales. Whether you embrace the speed and precision of Light or the raw control and power of Gravity, your choices will influence the battlefield and the universe itself.
Shifting Balance

In Warped Universe the choices players make, and the missions they take have an ever changing effect on the state of the seasons system and gameplay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0bbeac853a87ece348b0440c5543f48c71c6ae39.jpg[/img]
The star in the center of the map will show the current balance of Gravity and Light, the effects of which include changing movement speed, jump distance, how skills function, damage, resistances, and more. In the most extreme cases of imbalance, Void enemies will even receive a hefty damage buff. It’ll be up to players to decide whether they want to keep the balance or push it to one side or the other. You may want high gravity to take advantage of a certain loadout and skills, while others may prefer light or to pull things back to the center. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f7f2413e08c551bf00dc26cbfdaf11c0e31ba570.jpg[/img]
The way in which players direct the balance will come in the form of completing missions assigned to either the Luminaries or Foundationalists. Farms, Housing, and Factory missions push balance towards gravity, while Power, Research, and Space Port missions lean towards the Light. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/04e11fbfa8e1f8e75a667385acfe3390f17b0e35.jpg[/img]
These of course aren't the only mission types you’ll find on the System Map. There are also Explore missions, which are needed to open up the map to find new potential resources. In Pylon missions, players build and defend a network of pylons responsible for creating a safe zone required to begin mining resources or to build a new planet. Residuum missions are escort missions retrieving and transporting Residuum back to Nexus Station. Finally there are the Void Tear missions. Void Tears are a constant threat in the Warped Universe. If a Void Tear isn't closed in time, it can destroy a facility and set back all of the progress made by players. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f395f9d50f7f0f1e831dde46533ae248fb241c59.jpg[/img]
It will be up to you and the other inhabitants of Warped Universe to decide how much gets explored, which facilities are built, and what is saved. 
[h3]
The Choice is Yours.[/h3]

notes.title: The Space Game
notes.content:
"Time can move slower out there, if you want. This reality is not exactly the same as what we’re used to back home. I prefer to watch closely and plan my moves. Trouble is, in that mode of consciousness the void has time to plan its moves as well. Think about what they might do. You should know their strategies. They are likely your own. Outmaneuver, outgun, and for Oracle’s sake use cover. You won’t be covering as much ground as other missions, but it may feel like it.”
-Orin

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[h2]Space Combat in Warped Universe[/h2]
Once again, the choice is yours. In the interplanetary battlefield, movement takes place over vast distances rather than tight confines. Sweeping maneuvers may be useful but must always be purposeful. 

[h3]Think Fast, Act Faster[/h3]
In action space combat, one is always both predator and prey. Focus on a single target and your flank could be fully exposed. Prioritizing defensive maneuvers may sacrifice opportunities that would otherwise bring about a swift resolution. Players must be both pilot and navigator if they want to return to Nexus Station in triumph. Those excelling in rapid reactions will enjoy everything that action space combat has to offer.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d235be4b809175b0420d18c6727a01cfe9c6e21d.jpg[/img]
[h3]Limited Turns Require Meaningful Choices[/h3]
Turn-based space combat takes tactical vision and careful consideration. Time is no longer the enemy, rather the limited capabilities of rapid directional changes and high speed propulsion. 

Your enemy will take advantage of the same dilated time mechanic to actively thwart your efforts at every turn. Taking place on a hexagonally divided map, three dimensional space is visualized on a single plane. A considered approach to combat on such a playing field will be a vital component of the player’s strategy, and a major determinant of success.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/56854031ee627d31cf950be9d9d4d36b9b9161a7.jpg[/img]
Choice is the name of the game. Whether it’s turn-based or third-person action, you get to choose how you face each challenge in the Warped Universe.

[h3]Shared Systems, Unique Experiences[/h3]
No matter how you play, the core mechanics remain consistent. Equipment loadouts, upgrades, and abilities function across both modes, allowing you to seamlessly switch between styles depending on the mission or your preferred playstyle.
[h2]
The Choice is Yours[/h2]

notes.title: The Ground Game
notes.content:
“Listen up Freshprint. You’re gonna be in a big place without much help. The structures are stable but have lots of nooks and crannies for these beetle boys to crawl out of. You gotta get in and get out. Hit your objectives and get to the extraction point. They’ll usually be in groups but don’t think one of those bastards won’t sit and watch his buddies evaporate while he waits patiently for you to let your guard down. In, out. Kapiche?”
-Vanir

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[h2][b]Ground Combat in Warped Universe[/b][/h2]
Choice is the name of the game. Turn-based or action, on the ground or in space. You get to choose how you face each challenge in the Warped Universe.
Whether you're engaging in methodical, strategic encounters through turn-based combat or diving into the chaos of real-time action, the battlefield is yours to control. But each mode brings its own strengths and challenges.

[h3][b]Two Ways to Fight[/b][/h3]
In turn-based, every move counts, positioning, resource management, and ability combinations determine the outcome of each battle. Take the time to analyze enemy positioning, set up combos, and maximize your advantage. How you deal with environmental hazards and cover will play a key role in ensuring you complete your objectives. 

In action gameplay, however, there are no turns, no waiting, just pure movement and instinct. Battles are fast, fluid, and driven by player skill. If you can’t sneak up on your foes to take advantage of the first move, you’ll have to dodge as much incoming fire as you can to survive. Momentum is your greatest weapon.

[h3][b]Shared Systems, Unique Experiences[/b][/h3]
No matter how you play, the core mechanics remain consistent. Equipment loadouts, upgrades, and abilities function across both modes, allowing you to seamlessly switch between styles depending on the mission or your preferred playstyle.


[b]The Choice is Yours [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/e8f9a05b1a81f96876d345e67f6ced1a8bab2c5b.png[/img]

notes.title: Space At Your Pace
notes.content:
[i][h3]Not only is matter and energy altered in the warped universe, one’s perception of chronicity can be commanded in unexpected ways. Unfettered by the biological limitations of synaptic impulse potential, a mind can choose to move the echo in a more natural way, or process inputs in a state which may feel that time itself is standing still.[/h3][/i]

Drawing from our passion for diverse gaming experiences, we have developed an innovative design that integrates multiple genres within a single environment. This allows players to select their mission and then choose their preferred gameplay style, whether real-time action or turn-based strategy. Both genres utilize the same weapons, skills, damage systems, and mechanics, creating a fluid transition that enhances immersion, increases engagement, and broadens appeal.

[h3]Real-Time Action[/h3]
As a third-person action shooter, both as a character on the ground, or a ship up in space, this gameplay style caters to fast-paced thrill-seekers.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3a8f18e686f71ebb2168028c63e6489f0ef2cc62.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/c92a9941f4a140c46726ca3fe3e5ddff3a655d94.jpg[/img]

[h3]Turn-Based Strategy[/h3]
This top-down game style is ideal for players who prefer a more tactical approach. Utilizing action points and dice rolls to determine the outcomes of your missions. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/1f1397e066945ed3c0752efb6ffbad56aefea43f.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/ab09972be0dfffc05bb28b3d4a421f06be87a817.jpg[/img]
[h3]Play Your Way[/h3]
By allowing players to select how they engage with each mission, Warped Universe caters to a wide range of playstyles while encouraging collaboration across the community. This innovative approach draws on the preferred mechanics of popular real-time games like Fortnite and Helldivers 2, as well as successful turn-based strategy mechanics found in Dungeons and Dragons and XCOM, making Warped Universe appeal to an audience with diverse gaming preferences.
